reason: Plate IV draws the 1935-36 excavation grid, the Harappa II structures of Mound II, the Mound II contours and Pir's tomb. None of these could be identified in the imagery as a point: the grid pegs and excavated walls do not survive, the mound surface is broken by trees and its foot is cut by modern fields and a road, and no structure matching the tomb was found. The auxiliary Plates I and III add only the contours of Mounds I and III, the tomb and Majumdar's trenches, which fail in the same way, so no chain reaches three usable features.

candidates_considered.feature: Pir's tomb (drawn near the top of Plate IV, and on Plates I and III as a small oval or rectangle with a grave bar inside, about 4 m across at the Plate I scale)
candidates_considered.why: the only built feature on the plan. Wayback releases 10, 31026, 2168, 20753 and 16749 (2014-2022) show a ring about 20 m across at z18 pixel (614, 488) of the current mosaic frame, near where the tomb should lie relative to the bare ground; it is five times the drawn size, has a tree or dark fill at its centre, and is not visible from release 45441 (2022) onward. I could not identify it as the tomb, and no small building appears near it in any release

candidates_considered.feature: excavation grid pegs (circled intersections, rows 3-11, columns B-G)
candidates_considered.why: survey pegs of 1935-36; nothing at regular 100 ft spacing is visible in any release

candidates_considered.feature: Harappa II walls, drains and trench outlines of Mound II
candidates_considered.why: backfilled or eroded; no rectilinear walls or trench cuts in the bare ground in releases from 2014 to 2026

candidates_considered.feature: Mound II contours (5, 7 1/2, 10, 15, 20 and 23 ft), including the deep re-entrant on the north side and the southern lobe
candidates_considered.why: the imagery shows an uncultivated area with scattered trees whose edges follow field boundaries, a track and the diagonal road, not the contours; no corner, re-entrant or extremity of a contour can be placed to 12 m
no elevation information in the imagery

candidates_considered.feature: auxiliary Plate I, 'Chanhu-daro: contour map of the site' (PDF page index 361): contours of Mounds I, II and III, Pir's tomb, the site grid
candidates_considered.why: rendered at 300 dpi and examined. Its features are the same kinds as Plate IV's; it draws no road, canal, village or building other than the tomb. The three uncultivated patches in the imagery (north, centre and south-west of the diagonal road) match the relative layout of Mounds III, II and I, which locates the site, but no point on them can be placed to 12 m

candidates_considered.feature: auxiliary Plate III, 'Chanhu-daro: Mounds II and III' (PDF page index 365): Majumdar's trenches across Mound III, the tomb, trenches of Mound II
candidates_considered.why: rendered at 300 dpi and examined; Majumdar's 1930 trenches leave no linear depression that can be followed in the imagery, and the tomb fails as above

candidates_considered.feature: auxiliary Plate II, 'Chanhu-daro: Mound I' (PDF page index 363)
candidates_considered.why: contours and structures of Mound I only; same failure

notes: The site lies about 60 m west-south-west of the published coordinates: three uncultivated patches either side of a diagonal road, with a walled modern compound to the west. Zoom 19 returns placeholder tiles here, and zoom 18 Wayback releases older than 45441 are not served, so the older imagery was examined at zoom 17. The Mackay 1943 scan has no text layer. Plates II, III and IV carry the annotation 'MAG. NORTH NOV. 2ND 1935' with a north arrow, and Plate I a north arrow; these came into view in overview renders and I did not read their directions or use them. A trial overlay of Plate I at the scale-bar scale and unrotated (page up on image up), made only to test whether the ring could be the tomb, placed the three contour groups over the three patches but gave no point that could be identified independently.
